If sentiment is positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to capture upward momentum.

If sentiment is negative (≤-0.33) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid overestimating downside risk.

If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and forecast is trending upward, apply a 1–2% downward correction in mid horizon (8–15 days) to prevent overcorrection.

If sentiment is neutral and forecast is trending downward, apply a 1–2% upward correction in mid horizon (8–15 days) to avoid premature capitulation.

In late horizon (16–30 days), if sentiment is positive and forecast is above 70, reduce by 0.5–1.0% to reflect diminishing momentum.

In late horizon (16–30 days), if sentiment is negative and forecast is below 65, increase by 0.5–1.0% to reflect potential reversal.
